## Reject oversized fixed-width DER integers

Fixed-width DER decoding copies an ASN.1 INTEGER's content octets into a fixed-size byte array. Before this change an oversized INTEGER computed its offset with `saturating_sub` and then panicked while copying too many bytes into the array.

## Fix

Check the content length before copying:
- content that fits is right-aligned as before;
- a canonical positive INTEGER with its top bit set carries one leading sign octet, so content exactly one octet wider than the target is accepted with that octet stripped;
- anything wider is rejected (`None` / `Tag::Integer.length_error()` at the call site) instead of unwinding.

## Tests

Added a regression test that decodes a 17-byte INTEGER as `U128` without panicking, and one for the sign-octet form.

    cargo test --all-features uint::encoding::der::test -- --exact
